ui_bugs.issue:
CRITICAL COMPILE ERROR: React Hook 'useMemo' is called conditionally (after the early return on line 301: `if (!ch || !ref_) return
Summoning…
;`). useMemo is invoked on line 310 — this violates the react-hooks/rules-of-hooks ESLint rule and CRA treats it as a build-blocking error. The webpack-dev-server error overlay covers every page in the app, blocking all clicks (login button, create-campaign modal, every nav button). Fix: move the `const sentence = useMemo(...)` block ABOVE the `if (!ch || !ref_) return ...` early return on line 301, so the hook is always called in the same order. Same pattern likely applies to any other hooks added below the early return in this file (audit lines 290-330 and the Anime5e builder section).

rca of the issue:
Root cause: in /app/frontend/src/components/SystemCharacterBuilders.jsx the CypherBuilder component places an early return guard `if (!ch || !ref_) return
Summoning…
;` on line 301 before calling `useMemo` on line 310. React's Rules of Hooks require all hooks to be invoked in the exact same order on every render — calling useMemo only after a guard return means on the first render (when ch is null) useMemo is skipped, and on later renders it runs, which the eslint-plugin-react-hooks rule flags as an error. CRA's default webpack config promotes ESLint errors to compile failures and renders the red error overlay (iframe#webpack-dev-server-client-overlay) on top of every page in the app. That overlay is z-index ~9999 and intercepts pointer events, which is why every Playwright click times out with 'iframe id=webpack-dev-server-client-overlay intercepts pointer events'. Reproduction: 1) navigate to https://rules-forge.preview.emergentagent.com/auth?mode=login 2) observe the overlay containing the eslint message about 'React Hook useMemo is called conditionally' at SystemCharacterBuilders.jsx:310:20 3) any click attempt is intercepted. Mitigation: hoist the useMemo call (and any other hooks below the early return) to the top of the component body, before the guard return; if the memoised value depends on `c` which is only defined after `ch` is loaded, use optional chaining inside the memo body and let it return an empty sentence when ch is null.
